_doc: Ask AI over the journey contract (P10) — every number the answer engine uses lives here. Loaded by ask_ai/settings.py. Env ASK_AI_MODEL overrides llm.model at runtime (ops); everything else changes here.

context._doc: Character budget for what the model is shown. Account scope adds, in order: journey summary, row, investment priority, Power-of-1, investment cost (only when the question is investment-shaped -- scope.investment_phrases), episodes newest-first, evidence index, then the narrative, then role evidence. The narrative comes AFTER the episodes on purpose: its sentences carry episode ids, so it teaches the model what to cite, and any of its sentences whose episodes did not fit the budget are stripped before it is shown -- a sentence the model cannot legally cite must not be put in front of it, or the whole answer is dropped by the citation rule. Portfolio scope adds: portfolio summary, then -- only when the question is investment-shaped -- portfolio-level priority/Power-of-1/measured-ROI/investment-cost totals, then one row per account (each carrying its own compact priority). The first block that would overflow the budget is cut; only ids actually shown to the model are citable.

conversation._doc: In-session multi-turn continuity. The CLIENT holds the turns — nothing is persisted server-side, and this is NOT the (separate, deferred) cross-session memory feature. Each ask may carry `history`: the prior turns of the SAME conversation, oldest first. Only the last max_turns are read; each turn's question and answer are truncated to question_chars / answer_chars and the whole recap is hard-capped at max_chars. The recap is shown to the model under CONVERSATION SO FAR — OUTSIDE the CONTEXT BLOCKS and therefore outside Context.citable, so it is structurally uncitable: it is a record of what was said, not evidence. It disambiguates what the new question means; it never supplies a fact. follow_up_inherits_account: when a question names no account and no portfolio phrase, inherit the previous turn's account rather than falling back to the portfolio — that fallback is arbitrary, the live subject of the conversation is not.

scope._doc: Without an account_id the question is read for scope: an account name from the portfolio in the text selects that account; otherwise these phrases (or no match at all) mean portfolio. investment_phrases gates whether a portfolio question also pulls priority/Power-of-1/measured-ROI totals (account scope always includes the per-account versions — one account is cheap).
